summary: TerraCosmic is an interactive planetary exploration platform that identifies and ranks Earth analog sites most similar to target environments on the Moon and Mars — directly supporting future mission site selection. The system streams real geophysical telemetry from two authoritative open sources: NASA POWER (surface temperature, solar flux, wind speed — full 2025 annual dataset) and OpenTopoData ASTER 30 m DEM (terrain elevation, slope, and roughness computed from five-point spatial gradients). A FastAPI backend applies physics-based scoring — slope-range similarity, diurnal thermal range, solar energy density, and median-absolute-deviation anomaly detection — across a systematic 30-cell global Earth grid. Results are ranked and surfaced on a React/TypeScript mission dashboard featuring an interactive 3D CesiumJS Earth viewer, side-by-side Moon and Mars factor frameworks, site comparison tools, and exportable mission reports. A live Gemini-powered voice agent (TERION) allows fully hands-free exploration via natural language commands. By grounding planetary analog research in real, continuously refreshed Earth data rather than static assumptions, TerraCosmic makes the search for safe, resource-rich landing sites faster, more transparent, and open to anyone.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?

TerraCosmic is a full-stack planetary mission intelligence platform built to identify, score, and visualize Earth analog sites — locations on our planet whose geology, terrain, and climate most closely mirror target conditions on the Moon or Mars.

The platform operates in three integrated layers:

1 — Real-Data Screening Engine (FastAPI backend) Systematically samples a 30-cell global Earth grid, concurrently querying:

  • NASA POWER — full 2025 daily surface temp, wind speed, solar irradiance per location
  • OpenTopoData ASTER 30 m DEM — slope °, roughness m, local relief via 5-point finite-difference gradient math

Each location is scored against planetary reference parameters, ranked, and anomaly-flagged using MAD (median absolute deviation) statistics.

2 — Immersive Mission Dashboard (React + CesiumJS) 3D interactive Earth globe, ranked candidate lists with real measurements, multi-factor framework panels, site comparison modals, and exportable mission reports.

3 — TERION Voice AI Agent (Google Gemini Live) Fully hands-free navigation via natural language — "Survey Moon South Pole", "Compare landing sites", "Show water-ice map".
